verdict: Sections 2.1 to 2.3 are now numerically sound: every PRISMA count (9,256; 2,794; 6,039; 2,910; 3,129; 2,541; 741; 588; 1,800; 39/1,066/695; 64; 17 = 9+3+2+2+1; 3; 44 = 19+21+3+1; 23 core / 21 supporting), every search date and version, the calibration set (48), the rescue sweep (125), the saturation rule (eight), the retrieval routes (five), the decision-log range (D-001 to D-166) and the QA gate (sum of QA1 to QA4 at least 3.0) match prisma_counts.txt, searchlog.txt, codebook.txt and the decision log, and all 44 rows of Table 2 (labels S1 to S44, references [35] to [78], authors, years, titles and stream assignments) match studies_brief.txt exactly, with the stream sizes 12/5/8/5/5/9 summing to 44. The items that must be fixed before submission are the leftover orphan paragraph at the start of 2.3.7, the 'seven questions correspond one to one' contradiction with the six SRQs, the pointer to a non-existent threats-to-validity section, the overstated sentinel diagnosis (one miss is still an open item, two have other causes), the 422-versus-423 within-source duplicate arithmetic, the missing lifecycle component in the Req 1 definition, and the stale 2.1 list of review areas (Trusted Computing, multi-party trust governance) that no longer matches the six streams. Citation relevance in 2.1 and 2.2 is acceptable (background references [1]–[34] are used for context only), with one uncited empirical claim in 2.2.4 to soften and cite; once the listed fixes and the explicit checkpoint limitation are applied, this part of the chapter is ready for submission.
